To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

pentapeptide and larger palindromes with different secondary structures are present in proteins, they are not associated with the regular secondary structure, they are buried or exposed to the solvent and they are present in different protein families.

pentapeptide and long palindromes occur in all the major protein families and are not associated with specific secondary structures, are exposed to the solvent and interact with catalytic residues or ligands in proteins.

the palindrome sequences are associated with the secondary structural elements, have different solvent accessibility values, are associated with different number of residue neighborhood contact, interact with catalytic residues, ligands or metal ions in protein and are distributed in a relatively large number of protein families.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural, sequence and functional properties of pentapeptide and larger palindrome sequences in proteins.
the identification and analyses of the pentapeptide palindromes with known secondary structure in proteins.

the identification, characterization and analysis of the pentapeptide palindromes and large palindrome sequences in proteins and their association with the secondary structure conformation and other structural properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
palindromes can be found in proteins and they are important for the structure and function of proteins.
palindromes have different properties in proteins and may be associated with different functions in proteins.
palindromes can be either buried in a hydrophobic environment or exposed to solvent and may be important for function and stability in the corresponding protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
palindromes with different structural characteristics are present in proteins, and they may play important roles in protein function.
palindromes of different lengths in proteins have a diverse set of structural properties and are distributed in different protein families.
pentapeptide and larger palindromes can occur in proteins in different secondary structure conformation and may be important for protein stability and function.
The main takeaway from our work is that

palindromes of a given length in proteins are associated with different structural properties and amino acid residue preferences, which are not observed for the corresponding palindromes with the same length in nucleic acids.
palindromes can be found in all types of secondary structure conformations and in all protein folds.
palindromes can occur in any protein and are not limited to any specific protein family or protein function.
